messages:
marta: kicking off a speculative-decoding bring-up for llama3-70b q4 (new quant) this morning. baseline runs completed overnight without spec.

marta: plan is two-stage: fast model = vicuna-13b-q4, slow model = llama3-70b-q4, speculative p_keep sweep (0.6,0.7,0.8). small eval set (5k prompts) + live canary.

marta: immediate observation: overall token throughput improves, but we're seeing 200-400ms p99 spikes on some prompts when KV-cache warms while a speculative window is active. seems correlated to long recent-context prompts.

sanjeev: can you paste the config you ran? curious about max_fast_len and batching.

marta: sure, current test config:

```yaml
speculative:
  enabled: true
  fast_model: "vicuna-13b-q4"
  p_keep: 0.7
  max_fast_len: 32
  max_speculative_tokens: 48
  fallback_on_mismatch: true
```

kevin: runtime note: when the fast model's KV cache is small (short max_fast_len) and slow model needs to load larger KV pages, we can get a brief mutex on the device->host memcpy path. that shows up as a tail spike.

kevin: also saw increased GPU memcpy contention on hosts with mixed quant kernels (q4 vs q8). should try isolating a machine with homogeneous kernel set.

liz: for quality, how are you measuring regressions? we need both automatic metrics and manual inspection for hallucination/safety.

marta: eval harness used: our evals repo with 5k prompts (mix: 60% dialog, 30% reasoning, 10% code). metrics: exact-match (QA), Rouge-L (summaries), and our newer response-safety heuristic + toxicity filter.

marta: quick numbers (p95/p99 latency, quality delta vs baseline no-spec):
- p95 latency: -18%
- p99 latency: +12% (spike cases)
- avg tokens/sec: +24%
- QA EM: -0.9 pts (at p_keep 0.7)
- Rouge-L: -0.4 pts
- Safety flag rate: +0.2% (more low-confidence outputs)

sanjeev: interesting. small quality hit but big throughput gain. need to understand whether EM drop concentrates on reasoning prompts or short QA. can you run bucketed analysis?

marta: yes, preliminary bucket shows most EM drop on multi-step reasoning prompts with long context. single-turn factoid QA largely unaffected.

kevin: hypothesis: speculative tokens get accepted too aggressively when fast model is overconfident on early tokens but collapses later -> mismatch. we should try lowering p_keep and increasing max_fast_len tradeoffs. also add a fast-model calibration pass (temperature tweak or prompting).

liz: from ops side, we should gate canary traffic behind a fallback policy: if mismatch rate > 1% in 1k requests, auto-disable spec for that route. also add tracing hook to capture mismatch sequences for later error analysis.

marta: agreed. next experiments:
- sweep p_keep {0.6,0.65,0.7}
- try max_fast_len {16,32,64}
- run on homogeneous kernel hosts (kevin)
- add fast-model temp 0.8 vs 1.0 check
- run full 50k eval set focused on reasoning

bench-bot: upload complete: s3://redwood-bench/eng-ml/1765123456/speculative-runs/ (CSV + traces).

sanjeev: for logging, can we add a small reward-weighted metric: accept-rate * downstream-qa-EM to capture effective utility?

marta: good idea. I'll compute accept_rate and weighted EM in the next run.

kevin: timeline: i'll provision 4 homogeneous hosts today and run the kernel-isolated sweep. expecting results ~6-8h.

liz: i'll add the canary fallback policy and tracing. set threshold at 1% mismatch and retention 7 days for traces.

marta: thanks. i'll kick off sweeps once kevin confirms hosts. will post quick summary + top 20 mismatch traces here.

sanjeev: one more note — include a tiny human-eval set (50 prompts) targeted at hallucinations; have a pair review mismatches to triage whether it's quality regression vs prompt distribution shift.

marta: added. wrapping up for now, will post updates. :thumbsup:

kevin: :rocket:

bench-bot: ci-checks passed for speculative experiment run 1765123456.
